title: Probabilistic per-request cost & latency attribution (queryable economic cube)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current breakdown service materializes deterministic cost and latency aggregates but fails to capture uncertainty from sampling, partial caches (prefix/KV hits), and model-fallback routing. This results in noisy per-route and per-customer reports and opaque numbers for customers and SREs.

Goal: Build a complementary attribution layer that computes probabilistic per-request cost and latency attributions, stores marginal distributions and confidence intervals in a denormalized, queryable economic cube (time x customer x route x model variant). The cube should support both streaming updates (near realtime) and batched reconciliation with deterministic ground truth nightly rolls.

Scope: prototype the attribution algorithm (probabilistic apportionment & uncertainty propagation), design the cube schema, implement streaming enrichment job (Kafka -> Flink or Beam), materialize to BigQuery/ClickHouse, expose efficient APIs for Console and billing insights, and end-to-end tests and dashboards. This ticket covers initial prototype, integration tests, and a lightweight Console API for SLO/billing drilldown. Follow-ups will harden SLA and cross-region reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype job ingests request-level telemetry + routing decisions and emits probabilistic attributions (cost and latency distribution) for each request
Economic cube schema defined and documented with expected row cardinality and retention
Streaming enrichment pipeline implemented that writes provisional attribution rows to the cube within 2 minutes of request ingestion at 10k rps sustained (perf target for prototype)
Nightly reconciliation job that replaces provisional rows with deterministic ledger rows and computes reconciliation deltas
Console API endpoints to fetch time-windowed per-route/per-model/per-customer mean cost, p50/p90 latency and 95% confidence intervals
End-to-end test harness and synthetic workload demonstrating attribution accuracy within 5% of deterministic baseline on average, and plausible CI coverage
technical_notes: Attribution model: mixture of deterministic apportionment (explicit resource tags) and probabilistic split where resource ownership is ambiguous (e.g., shared batching, multi-model routing). Use bootstrap & analytic variance propagation to compute CI.
Streaming stack: prefer Flink on Dataproc/EMR or Beam (Dataflow) depending on team availability. Kafka topic is telemetry.v2.request-events; enrichments must be idempotent using request_id as key.
Storage: ClickHouse for low-latency Console queries (day-level high-cardinality), daily roll-forward into BigQuery for long-term reporting and billing reconciliation.

Schema: denormalized rows with flat dimensions (date_hour, customer_id, route_id, model_variant, region, pricing_tier) and metrics as stringified JSON blob for distribution summary (mean, count, sum, sumsq, percentile-approx sketch reference).

Cost model inputs: token counts (prompt/completion), model GPU seconds estimate, kernel-selection multiplier, batch amortization factor, network egress estimate. Join keys must preserve privacy constraints for Private customers.
Backfill strategy: reprocess 7 days on schema changes; reconcile provisional vs deterministic via delta table with mutation-friendly store (BigQuery MERGE or ClickHouse replacingMergeTree).
Query API: GraphQL or REST route /api/insights/econ-cube with query params (start,end,dimensions,metrics,confidence). Cache hot slices with LRU TTL in Console backend.
Metrics and SLOs: streaming job lag <120s, cube query latency <200ms for single-customer single-route 24h range, reconciliation job <6h for 24h window.
Privacy/Compliance: strip PII from telemetry before cubing; obey customer opt-outs for usage analytics; honor region-bound data residency for Private deployments.

notes_and_risks: High-cardinality customers + many per-customer routes could create hot partitions in ClickHouse; mitigate via sharding and TTLs for provisional rows.
Probabilistic attribution introduces non-intuitive numbers for customers — must include UI copy explaining confidence intervals and nightly reconciliation behavior.
Reconciliation deltas may trigger billing questions; coordinate with finance and support before broad rollout.
Edge case: cached responses (100% KV hit) must be attributed near-zero model cost but non-zero latency; ensure the model for latency splits caches vs compute is validated.
